description.p: Jorvik is a Matrix client that arranges a homeserver the way a chat app should feel: Spaces are servers, rooms are channels, and end-to-end encryption is on by default.
It is built on Matrix, an open network: an account on matrix.jorvik.app can talk with people on other Matrix servers, and the same account works in other Matrix apps.
Features:

ul.li: Spaces and channels, with nested subspaces
End-to-end encrypted messages and encrypted media
Voice channels, and calls from a profile
Custom emoji
Desktop notifications and an unread badge on the tray icon

screenshot.caption: A Space with its channels and a conversation

description.p: Choose exactly who sees the game you're playing, and Steam games show their own icon.

ul.li: Activity privacy: choose exactly who sees what you're playing (friends, all spaces, small spaces only, or per space), hide specific games, and keep your status message separate. Activity is end-to-end encrypted and never stored in room history

It has its own page in Settings, Activity Privacy, in place of "Show the game I'm playing", and a switch in the status menu. If you had that on, it stays on, now shared with your friends and spaces of up to 200 people
Steam games show their own icon next to your name and on your profile. It's end-to-end encrypted too, and nobody's app contacts Steam to show it
The status menu says what Online and Idle do: Online goes idle by itself while you're away, and Idle stays until you change it

description.p: Show the game you're playing, and see the status people set.

ul.li: New in Settings, Privacy & Safety: "Show the game I'm playing". It's off until you turn it on. While it's on, your status shows the game you're playing, from Steam or a list of popular games, and only its name is shared. The Flatpak and Snap versions can't see other programs, so it isn't available there
The status people set for themselves now shows in the member list and on their profile
Copying messages copies just the messages. Before, the emoji of the buttons and reactions under them came along

description.p: Notifications open their chat, and stickers show up.

ul.li: Clicking a notification opens the chat it's about, in whichever Space it's in, and brings Jorvik back from the tray
Stickers sent from other Matrix apps show in the chat. Before, they only marked it unread
If this session is signed out from another device, Jorvik goes to the sign-in screen and says why, instead of showing old chats

description.p: Removing old sessions works in long lists, and the Linux packages bring their sound library along.

ul.li: Sign out next to a session in Settings, Devices opens its confirmation right under that session. In a long list it used to open out of sight at the top, so the button seemed to do nothing. Enter now confirms the password
The .deb and .rpm packages depend on ALSA, so Jorvik also starts on minimal systems that don't have it yet

description.p: Sign in to any Matrix server, and chat.jorvik.app on phones.

ul.li: The gear on the sign-in screen opens Server settings, where you can sign in to or create an account on another Matrix server. Jorvik keeps it until you change it. Voice channels, calls and GIFs still need a server that runs Jorvik's voice service
Sign out, deleting a message, leaving and the other questions use Jorvik's own confirmation, which works in every browser
When the server can't be reached, sign-in says so plainly
On a phone, chat.jorvik.app has a layout of its own: your spaces and chats, a chat full screen, and swipes to go back or to see who's there
Push notifications for chat.jorvik.app on phones and in browsers: turn them on in Settings, Notifications. On an iPhone, add Jorvik to the Home Screen first
Hold a message on a touch screen to open its menu
Dark mode add-ons no longer recolour Jorvik's own dark theme

description.p: Light mode that stays light.

ul.li: In light mode the app opens light, with no dark screens before you're signed in
The window's edges and the strip behind the window controls follow the theme, so light mode no longer flashes dark when the window is redrawn
Profiles and room details in the side panel are readable in light mode
The buttons on the sign-in and security screens are readable in light mode

description.p: Easier channel making, and invites by @name.

ul.li: A + at the top of a space's channel list creates a channel, for people who can add one
A new channel shows in its space straight away, as does one someone else adds, with no need to reload channels
Create channel in Server settings keeps settings open, and picks the new channel in the list, ready to move
Invite people on your server as just @name, and a mistyped name is caught instead of looking invited
Messages such as "Channels reloaded" show over settings instead of behind them
The badges room is no longer offered as a place to invite someone

description.p: Mark all as read, unread dots that clear, and encrypted spaces.

ul.li: Right-clicking @ or a space in the left rail offers Mark all as read
Only new messages mark a chat unread: a call being answered, a reaction or an edit no longer does
Opening a chat always clears its unread dot
New spaces are end-to-end encrypted by default, and an existing space can be encrypted in Server settings under Visibility
Imported channels, voice channels included, are encrypted by default

description.p: Video in calls, and end-to-end encrypted calls.

ul.li: Turn your camera on in a voice channel or call, and people with their camera on get big tiles above everyone else
Settings, now called Voice and video, picks your camera and can preview it
Calls in encrypted chats are end-to-end encrypted, voice, video and screen share alike: only the people in the call can hear and see it
DMs are encrypted, and new voice channels now are too; an existing channel can be encrypted from its call
A call says whether it is end-to-end encrypted, and everyone in an encrypted call needs this version or the web app
On macOS, Jorvik says why it asks for the camera and microphone

description.p: A line where new messages begin, dates on messages, and fixes.

ul.li: A red line marks where new messages begin, and a bar jumps to it (also Shift+Page Up)
A line marks where each day begins, messages say "Yesterday at 14:02" or the date, and hovering a time shows the full date
Messages are no longer marked as read while you are away from Jorvik
A chat whose messages fit on the screen loads its older messages
Older messages that finish loading after you switch chats stay in their own chat
A profile's "Last active" time keeps counting while someone is idle
Channel and chat info have a close button
A profile's menu is no longer cut off in a narrow window
Security fixes from Electron 44.7.0

description.p: Text formatting, a quick switcher, unread badges in the rail, and fixes.

ul.li: Messages can use bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers, code, quotes, lists, headings and links
Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) jumps to any channel, DM or space, and the Up arrow edits your last message
Each space and your DMs show unread messages and mentions in the left rail
People on the same server can be mentioned as just @name
A crossed-out bell marks chats set to Mute or Mentions only, and chat settings now hold that choice
A link whose text hides where it goes asks before opening
Settings list every keyboard shortcut
The chat header moves the window in long chats too
Clicking outside a dialog or the image viewer closes it, and checkbox labels can be clicked

description.p: Name badges, developer tools that stay closed, and fixes.

ul.li: Badges next to names: Staff, Bug Finder, Tester, Contributor and Early Supporter, given out by the server's badge managers from a profile
The developer tools stay closed unless turned on in Settings, Appearance
The top edge of the right-hand panel moves the window, as the chat header does
The menu on a channel inside a category is no longer hidden
Room settings show a room's own name, not one made up from its members

description.p: Security keys that work when you need them, and calls that show everyone.

ul.li: Calls show the picture of everyone in them, your own included
Names show plainly, without an @name added when two people share one
A new security key made in Settings works at the next sign-in, and a key that is not saved yet says so
Finishing setup after a key change no longer fails with a decryption error
The security key screens say what to do if you have lost your key
Signing up no longer shows an error while you wait for the verification email

description.p: Clearer names, and any chat can be deleted.

ul.li: Direct messages are named after the person, with their @name beside their display name
Any direct message can be deleted, including one the other person started
The security screens say which account you are signed in as
The Flatpak moves to the 26.08 runtime and asks for fewer permissions

description.p: Verification with other Matrix apps works, and a batch of new features.

ul.li: Your account gets cross-signing, so Element and other apps can verify it with your security key
Call someone from their profile, and invite them to a server or channel
Do Not Disturb, and an automatic Idle status
Trending and favourite GIFs
Link previews
Block and report people, and delete a server
A Flatpak build, and AppImage updates in place

description.p: The right panel is remembered separately for direct messages and servers.
Fixes encryption in direct messages, and a one-to-one conversation shows the other person's profile.
